name: bendith y mamau
text: bendith y mamau is a Welsh phrase meaning the blessings of the mothers. Speakers in Glamorganshire use it as a euphemism for the fairies. Welsh tradition more often calls those beings tylwyth teg. Users prefer the euphemism to avoid kidnapping and the fairies' mischief. Related lore also names a hound pack, cwn bendith y mamau, the dogs of the blessed ones. MacKillop treats that phrase under the entry c’wn annwn.

attributes.attribute: Welsh for the blessings of the mothers

okr.objective: bendith y mamau records the Glamorganshire euphemism for the fairies of Wales.
